newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICAN SUGAR STRIKE MIGHT END ON THURSDAY.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICAN SUGAR STRIKE MIGHT END ON THURSDAY.

text.p: A 15-day strike by thousands of South African sugar workers might end on Thursday if union members voted in favour of a draft agreement reached with management, a union official said on Wednesday.

Management and unions reached a draft agreement in the early hours of Wednesday morning to settle the strike which has crippled the South African sugar industry, a spokesman for Illovo Sugar Ltd and Tongaat-Hulett Ltd said.

A spokesman for the five unions taking part in the strike, Eric Botha, said if members agreed, the draft agreement could be signed on Thursday -- paving the way for a return to work of around 4,000 workers at 14 mills and refineries in the KwaZulu-Natal sugar producing region.
"If our members accept the offer that we will be putting to them today (Wednesday), we will sign the agreement at a meeting tomorrow morning".
Botha said the draft agreement included a wage increase of 11.5 percent backdated to April 1.
A spokesman for the two companies said he was hopeful that the draft agreement would be signed.

The sugar industry has estimated that it was losing some 83,500 tonnes of cane in production but the blow has been softened somewhat by the unions giving early warning of their impending industrial action.
An industry source said the unions gave notice six days before the strike of their intention to strike.
Millers were able to notify sugar growers not to deliver cane to the mills, the source said, adding that cane on the fields would only lose some sucrose content.
He said the loss in production could be made up by extending the crushing season -- which usually runs from the beginning of April to just after Christmas.
The sugar industry has declined to put a value to the production losses.
